chunks: 1039 - And ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah narrated from Zurārah from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the sick person: how should he perform sajdah?

He said: "On a khumrah, or on a fan, or on a siwāk that is raised up to him, and that is better than gesturing. The one who disliked sajdah on a fan only disliked it because of the idols that used to be worshipped besides Allah. And we have never worshipped other than Allah at all, so perform sajdah on the fan, on the siwāk, and on a piece of wood."

key_terms.الْإِيمَاءِ: gesturing in place of full physical sajdah
key_terms.الْمَرِيضِ: the sick person whose prayer method is being discussed
key_terms.خُمْرَةٍ: a small mat or prayer mat used for sajdah
key_terms.سِوَاكٍ: a tooth-stick or small stick that may be raised for sajdah
key_terms.عُودٍ: a piece of wood used as a surface for sajdah
key_terms.مِرْوَحَةٍ: a fan or palm-fiber fan used here as a surface for sajdah

ai.seo_question: How should a sick person perform sajdah according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains how a sick person may perform sajdah by using an object raised up to them, such as a khumrah, fan, siwāk, or wood. It indicates that actual placement for sajdah in this manner is better than mere gesturing, and it clarifies that any earlier dislike regarding prostration on a fan was tied to idol-related associations, not to the object itself.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1039 - Umar ibn Udhaynah narrated from Zurarah from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that he asked about how a sick person should perform prostration (Sujood).

Abu Ja'far said: "On a small mat (Khumrah), a fan (Miroohah), or a stick (Miswak) that is raised to them, and this is better than mere gesturing. The disapproval from some for prostrating on a fan was due to the idols that were worshiped besides Allah (swt). However, we have never worshiped anything besides Allah (swt), so prostrate on the fan, on the Miswak, or on a piece of wood."
